steps: Hold your non-dominant hand out in front of you as a flat hand, fingers together, palm facing down.
Shape your dominant hand into a flat hand too, with the fingers slightly bent and relaxed.
Bring the pinky edge of your dominant hand down onto the back of your non-dominant hand.
Brush your dominant hand across the back of the other hand in one short swipe, ending just past its edge.
Keep the wrist loose so the brush-off motion stays quick, light, and easy.
Keep a neutral or pleasant face, since this sign is about a low price, not something bad.
tip: One quick brush-off across a flat hand — picture wiping a price tag down to something small.

steps: Raise your dominant index finger to your lips, touching the fingertip to them lightly.
Point the finger slightly sideways so your palm faces your non-dominant side.
Push your hand forward several inches in one quick, firm motion.
Keep the finger stiff and the movement short, stopping cleanly at the end.
Pair the sign with a confident nod and steady eye contact when you want to affirm something.
tip: One production does heavy duty: it also covers sure, indeed, really, very, and you're welcome in context.

steps: Touch the fingertips of your dominant flat hand to your lips or chin, palm facing you.
Move your hand down and away from your face in one smooth arc.
As your hand travels, twist it so your palm rotates to face downward.
End with your hand open in front of your chest, palm facing down.
Wear a frown or scowl to match the meaning — the face carries the negativity.
tip: BAD is the mirror image of GOOD: same start at the mouth, but the palm twists down instead of up.

steps: Form both hands into A fists, with your thumbs tucked up along the fingers.
Press the two fists together in front of your chest, palms facing each other.
Keeping the fists touching, stir them in a flat horizontal circle, as if mixing a pot.
Make one full, smooth sweep of the circle in a single continuous movement.
Hold your torso relaxed and keep your eyes on your conversation partner.
tip: Start from the WITH sign — two fists pressed together — then stir. The circling motion is what says 'all of us as one.'

steps: Hold your dominant hand up beside your cheek as a fist, with the thumb sticking up like the letter A.
Keep the fist steady and flick the thumb upward in one quick, single motion.
Let the thumb pop up and freeze for a beat before relaxing the hand.
Make the motion short and decisive — one flick, not a repeated wiggle.
Keep a neutral, questioning face when you use it in a sentence like 'who else?'
tip: Lifeprint teaches OTHER and ELSE as the same sign: one quick thumb-flick up. Do it twice and you are signing TEN instead.

steps: Hold both hands out in front of your torso as flat hands, palms facing down.
Keep your fingers together and the hands roughly shoulder-width apart.
Move both hands straight downward a few inches in one smooth, even motion.
Keep the hands level with each other through the whole drop.
Hold a neutral, matter-of-fact expression, since this is a plain noun sign.
tip: This is Lifeprint's non-initialized PERSON sign — no P handshapes needed — and it doubles as the AGENT suffix in signs like TEACH-PERSON.

steps: Hold your dominant hand out in front of you, palm facing down, at about chest height.
Pat the air once downward, as if patting the head of a small child standing in front of you.
Shift your hand a few inches to the side and pat the air a second time.
Make each pat a single short, light dip of the hand.
Keep a warm, friendly face, since the sign conjures two little kids in front of you.
tip: Lifeprint's trick: one quick pat per child, two imaginary heads — that is what turns CHILD into KIDS without any extra sign.

steps: Close both hands into S fists, with your thumbs folded across your fingers.
Hold the fists in front of your chest with the thumb sides facing each other and the palms facing down.
Strike the knuckle sides of your fists together.
Hit them together a second time, as if knocking two stones against each other.
Keep the strikes crisp and close to your chest, letting the soundless knock carry the meaning.
tip: Knuckles-to-knuckles twice — the collision of the two S fists is what makes the stone 'hard.'
